note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Active runner with 2 weeks of right knee pain and clicking that starts after ~20 minutes of running; no rest pain or instability; brief initial swelling resolved with ice. Plan: activity modification, ice, NSAID (stronger agent prescribed), referral to physiotherapy; monitor for red flags.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain and clicking with exercise; occasional tingling in right toes after a run.
- Timeline:
  - Onset ~2 weeks ago after starting marathon training (~1 month ago).
  - Pain begins ~20 minutes into a run (~2.5–3 miles); worsening to the point she stopped her last run.
  - Initial mild swelling after the first run, resolved with ice; currently no swelling or pain at rest.
- Characteristics:
  - Location: Feels central but tends to the right (lateral) side of the right knee.
  - Triggers: Running; repetitive knee flexion/extension during ab workouts at the gym.
  - Relieving: Rest and ice; ibuprofen 400 mg PRN offers some relief.
  - Function: No issues with walking, stairs, or full range of motion; can fully flex and extend.
- Associated symptoms:
  - One episode of tingling in the right toes after a run, resolved; no persistent numbness/weakness.
  - Occasional sock indentations after prolonged standing.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No persistent swelling, redness, warmth, fever, or systemic symptoms.
  - No locking, no true giving way/instability, no back pain.
  - No calf pain; no color or temperature change in the lower legs.
  - No foot joint or arch pain; no difficulty walking on hard floors.

Past Medical History:
- Farsighted; status post LASIK surgery.
- Prior severe UTI episode (evaluated in ER; kidney stones were considered).
- Sports history: Plays ice hockey; fell months ago causing a large bruise (no ongoing joint issues reported).

Medications:
- Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed; route/frequency not fully documented.
- Naproxen (Aleve) used occasionally; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Vitamin D; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Melatonin; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Alprazolam (Xanax) occasionally for sleep; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not recorded.

Social History:
- Training for a marathon; runs up to 7–8 miles; gym a few times per week.
- Plays ice hockey.
- Occasional cannabis use (“smoke a joint”).
- Lives in London.
- Tobacco/alcohol use: Not recorded.
- Occupation: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Musculoskeletal/neurologic: Patient-reported full knee ROM; currently no swelling; no locking or instability; gait and stair use without pain.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Overuse-related right knee pain in a runner, most consistent with lateral knee overuse (iliotibial band friction syndrome) or patellofemoral pain syndrome; meniscal pathology less likely. Single transient episode of right toe tingling likely post-activity/footwear-related and resolved.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Iliotibial band friction syndrome (ITBFS): Supported by lateral-predominant pain starting after several miles with recent mileage increase and clicking with repetitive flexion/extension; opposed by initial mild swelling.
  - Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS): Supported by pain with running and crepitus/clicking during flexion/extension; opposed by lack of stair pain and pain not clearly anterior.
  - Meniscal pathology: Supported by clicking and transient swelling; opposed by no locking, full ROM, no distinct twisting injury, and progressive activity-related onset.

- Issue 1: Right knee pain with clicking, likely overuse (ITBFS vs PFPS).
  - Activity modification: Temporarily reduce running volume and intensity; avoid running through pain.
  - Symptomatic care: Continue ice therapy as frequently as practical.
  - Medications: Stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed to pharmacy; take with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen (avoid duplication). Specific drug/dose not documented.
  - Referral: Physiotherapy for detailed knee assessment and targeted rehab program.
  - Imaging: Consider only if symptoms persist or if physio assessment indicates (to evaluate cartilage/meniscus).
  - Red flags/urgent care: Return urgently for persistent/worsening swelling, heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.

- Issue 2: Transient right toe tingling post-run.
  - Assessment: Single episode, resolved; no persistent neurovascular deficits.
  - Plan: Monitor; ensure proper footwear and lacing. Seek care if tingling recurs persistently, is associated with weakness, color/temperature change, or spreads.

- Issue 3: NSAID use/safety.
  - Reinforce taking NSAIDs with food; avoid combining different NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen with prescribed NSAID).
  - Monitor for GI upset; stop and seek care for severe abdominal pain, black stools, or vomiting blood.

- General plan items:
  - Follow-up: With physiotherapy; clinic follow-up if wait is prolonged or if symptoms worsen despite measures.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not recorded; vitals and objective knee exam not recorded; detailed doses/routes/frequencies for several medications not documented; tobacco and alcohol use not recorded.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear history; no physical exam performed during this video consult.
